title: The Moat That Waited for a Wave
spine: A child's walk from the dune path to the water's edge, following the tide's row of gifts to the perfect castle spot, where a moat waits for the sea to fill it all by itself.

hero_name.role: The hero's name, used by Granny and the narrator

segments.text: The sand was warm before we even saw it. "Off we go, {hero_name}," said Granny, and her bucket went swing, swing, swing. Up the wooden path we climbed, up over the dunes, and the grass heads nodded at us. Whisper, whisper. Then — the whole beach! Gold as far as we could look. And there, down below, went a curly line of things the sea had left behind. Shells. Seaweed. Foam bubbles, winking in the sun. Granny stopped. She put her hands in her pockets, where her found shells rattled. "Now who," she said, "left a trail like that? And where does it go?"

"Toes in!" you shout, and off the path you hop. The sand is hot on top — hot, hot, hot! "Quick," says Granny, "push your toes down." Down you push, and — oh! Underneath, the sand is cool, like a secret waiting. "Well, would you look at that," says Granny. You wiggle-walk along the trail, past a white feather, soft as a whisper. Granny scoops up two handfuls of sand. One is dry — it slips away like sugar, fssst, through her fingers. One is damp — it holds its shape, like a little hill. "Now why," she says, turning her hands over, "does one run away and one stay put?" Ahead, the shells glint. Wink, wink. The trail curls on, down to the wet sand, and your toes are already going.

"Up high!" you shout, and up you climb, up among the nodding grass. Whisper, whisper. Granny pats the sandy hill. "The wind built this," she says. "And the grass holds it still, like fingers holding tight." You stand on top and — oh! You can see the whole trail at once, like a seagull would. A white feather. A round dark hole, where a crab lives. A spiral seashell, pink as a sunset. All in a row, pointing down, down, down to the wet sand. "There it is!" you shout. "The whole trail!" Granny's shells rattle in her pocket. "Now where," she says, "does it end?" Down you scramble, legs tickled by spiky grass, down to where the line goes on.

Down we went, onto the smooth wet sand. It was cool and firm under our toes. "The sea's doorstep," said Granny. "Best place to stand." Then we saw it. A round dark hole. And tiny footprints all around it, like a star. Out popped a little crab, the colour of sand. It ran sideways. It stopped. It looked at us. Then — zip! Back in its hole. "Oh!" we laughed. Granny rattled her pocket shells. "What did you find back there?" she asked. "Tell me on the way." Because look — the line of foam bubbles ended right here. And there stood the biggest sandcastle we had ever seen. A big kid waved a spare spade. "Want to help?" they called. "We need one more thing!"

"I'll drizzle!" said {hero_name}. The spade was heavy and good. Wet sand slid off it in lumpy ribbons. Plop. Plop. And the ribbons held their shape, right on top of the big castle. "My tower," said {hero_name}. The big kid dug the moat, round and round, deep and curly. Then we all sat back. And waited. One wave stopped far away. The next came closer. The next, closer still. "Here it comes," whispered Granny. And one foamy edge swirled right into the moat. Fizz! Bubbles everywhere! The castle stood dry inside. {hero_name} planted the spiral seashell on top, for a flag. On the way home, Granny held out a smooth little periwinkle. "That one's safe to take," she said. So we did.

"I'll dig!" said {hero_name}. The spade bit into the wet sand. Scrape. Scrape. Round and round the big castle went the moat, deep and curly, and {hero_name} patted the walls smooth. The big kid drizzled the towers. Plop. Plop. Then we all sat back at the sea's doorstep. And waited. One wave stopped far away. The next came closer. The next, closer still. "Here it comes," whispered Granny. And one wave slid all the way up and filled the moat. Fizz! Bubbles everywhere! The castle stood dry inside. {hero_name} planted the spiral seashell on top, for a flag. On the way home, Granny picked up a fan-ridged shell from the tideline. "That was once an animal's house," she said. "You may keep it." So we did.

gathered_but_unused: Sand is made of tiny pieces of rock and shell that the sea has rubbed and rolled until they became small and smooth.
The tide goes in and out, and when it goes out it leaves treasures behind on the wet sand.
Wet sand sticks together and dry sand falls apart, which is why sandcastle builders carry buckets of water.
A wave can slide all the way up the beach and fill a sandcastle moat all by itself.
Dunes are hills of sand made by the wind, and special grasses grow on them to hold the sand still with their long roots.
Sand feels warm on top where the sun has been shining, but cool and damp if you dig your toes down underneath.
Some holes in the sand belong to little animals like crabs, who dig down to stay cool and damp.
The sea makes a shushing sound as each wave slides up the sand and pulls the sand grains gently back down.
